transcript: The work gets done every day. Vantage keeps it on the record.
Today starts with what needs you: the work you hold, what’s due and what’s overdue.
Personnel lists every Marine’s billet, supervisor and roles.
A Marine’s page shows only what they shared, and opening it is logged.
Log what you did in one line.
Vantage reads the numbers. You check them and save.
Duty is scored by your Unit Instance’s published policy, and counts once a reviewer approves it.
Attach the certificate to the training it proves. Vantage checks the file is what it says it is.
Financial work comes to one queue. Claim a case and it’s yours.
Its written procedure shows the next step.
File each error report as it stood. Vantage shows what’s new, still open, reopened and resolved.
Every case is diagnosed by written rules, not AI, and every recommendation names its source.
Every report prints or files as a PDF: a Marine’s record, the unit’s output, its training and its duty.
The unit dashboard counts shared records only, and every figure opens the records behind it.
Each command runs its own Unit Instance, kept apart from every other.
Unit Managers govern it. Vantage Administrators run the service.
Press N from any page.
Type it the way you’d say it.
Vantage fills in the count, the dollar amount, the system and the date.
Look it over, fix anything that’s off, and save.
No connection? It saves on your device and syncs later.
Your section’s open work is all in one queue.
Claim a case and it moves to your list.
Claiming a case doesn’t give you credit. The work you log on it does.
The procedure shows the next step and only asks for what that step needs.
Enter what you found and Vantage does the math, showing every number it used.
If a step needs evidence first, it tells you up front.
Everything you do goes into the case history under your name.
If you hand the case off, you each keep credit for your own part.
The FMRA desk reference is built in, with a source for everything in it.
Enter the commitment, obligation, delivered and paid amounts.
Vantage shows what’s still open, what could be causing it, who can fix it, and what proves it’s fixed.
A dash on a report doesn’t mean zero. Mark it as “not shown.”
Open a case from here and the numbers carry over, along with where they came from.
Your record keeps three things separate.
Work you’re holding. That isn’t credit yet.
Work you contributed to, counted from the case itself.
Things you logged yourself.
A document only counts once, no matter how many entries it took.
From any case you worked, you can start a private draft using only your own facts.
Save it and it’s added to your record with a link to the case.
Report Studio helps you put what you’ve logged into your JEPES or FITREP.
Pick the period and the entries you want to cite.
Click any cited entry to check it while you write.
If one of those entries changes while you’re writing, it won’t save until you look at it again.
Each saved version is locked to exactly what it cited.
If you lead a section, Today shows your section first.
What’s unassigned, overdue, blocked, or waiting on someone else.
How many open commitments, undelivered orders and UMTs you have.
Workload shows who’s holding what, and explains what each number means.
These counts don’t measure effort. Zero logged doesn’t mean zero done.
Day one, you’ll get an email with your username and a link to set your password.
Today has a short checklist for your first week. Items check off as you do them.
Start by adding a passkey or an authenticator app to your account.
Check your profile and make sure your rank is right.
Log one thing you did. One line is enough.
By Friday, open Team to see your people, your chain of command, and shared goals.
When you save an entry, you pick who can see it.
Only me: nobody else can open it. Not your leaders, not the site owner.
My unit: it counts on the unit dashboard for leaders over that unit.
Every entry shows who can see it, right at the top.
Drafts and career plans are always private.
When a leader opens your record, that gets logged.
Bring in the spreadsheet your section already uses. Your original file isn’t changed.
Vantage reads the column headers and guesses what each one is. Fix any it got wrong.
You see a preview of every row before anything is saved.
Each row becomes an item in the queue, linked back to its row in the file.
Import the same file again and nothing gets duplicated.
The Analysis tab shows what your record actually says before you use it.
Hours, kilometers and dollars are kept separate and never added together.
The summary shows how often you log, your longest gap, and where your pace puts you.
Coverage points out entries missing details, so you can fix them before a report uses them.
Click any number on Today to see the entries behind it.
Record a counseling from the Marine’s page: what went well, what to work on, and goals.
Once it’s saved, it’s on their record with the date and your name.
They open it under Career and acknowledge it.
Acknowledging means they read it. It doesn’t mean they agree.
You both see the same record, marked acknowledged.
On first launch, create the owner account and your first unit.
The Owner console is where you manage settings, accounts, units, email, retention and backups.
Get settings right before anyone else signs in, starting with whether people can sign themselves up.
Build your chain of command. Teams go under their command, and permissions flow down, not up.
Add people by invite, by importing a roster, or by emailing everyone their sign-in details.
Retention is off until you turn it on, one record type at a time. Each schedule lists its authority.
Preview what would be deleted before anything runs.
A legal hold blocks any deletion it covers, even if a schedule says otherwise.
The privacy inventory is built from the live database, so it stays current.
Export it for your privacy impact assessment.
